# 01 · At a glance

Live hospital counts come from `data/territoryHospitals.json` (March 2026 CMS TEAM participant extract). Editorial context (Medicare population, HRRP, LEJR) is carried from the published Rainfall guide and is **not** recomputed from claims.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-glance
glance <- tibble::tibble(
  Signal = c("Mandated hospitals", "CBSAs", "Medicare beneficiaries", "HRRP", "Est. annual LEJR"),
  Value = c(
    as.character(SCOPE_N),
    as.character(SCOPE_CBSA_N),
    editorial$medicare,
    editorial$hrrp,
    editorial$lejr
  ),
  `Why it matters` = c(
    editorial$why_hospitals,
    paste("Largest CBSA:", top_cbsa, "(", top_cbsa_n, "hospitals)"),
    "Covered-lives scale",
    "Readmission pressure under episode accountability",
    "Volume concentration"
  )
)
knitr::kable(glance)
```

# 03 · Guide narrative (from the website TEAM report)


### Takeaways

- 164 hospitals — Territory 4 roster
- Florida 40 and Tennessee 30 lead
- Nashville CBSA: 19 TEAM hospitals
- HCA TriStar multi-site advantage
- AdventHealth Florida density

## What is Rainfall Territory 4 under CMS TEAM?

**Territory 4 (South & Midwest)** includes **164** mandated hospitals (**22.7%** of 721). States and territories: Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, Kentucky, Puerto Rico, Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan.

**Florida (40)** and **Tennessee (30)** dominate. The **Nashville–Davidson–Murfreesboro–Franklin** CBSA has **19** TEAM hospitals — a for-profit and regional-nonprofit battleground where HCA TriStar density is a defining feature of the Tennessee state guide.

Florida’s TEAM map is uneven: Jacksonville (13), Daytona/Deltona (8), Lakeland (5), and Fort Walton (5) appear, while much of Miami-Dade was **not** selected. Hospital executives should not assume “Florida = TEAM”; CBSA membership is the rule.

(Source: [CMS TEAM participant list (March 2026); Rainfall territoryHospitals.json.](https://www.cms.gov/priorities/innovation/innovation-models/team-model))

**Fast facts**

- 164 mandated hospitals (March 2026)
- Top states: Florida 40 · Tennessee 30 · Kentucky 17 · North Carolina 16 · Georgia 14 · Mississippi 12 · South Carolina 12
- Top CBSAs: Nashville 19 · Jacksonville 13 · Memphis 10 · Daytona/Deltona 8 · Greenville SC 8 · Lexington KY 7
- System signals: HCA (TriStar + Florida), AdventHealth, Ascension, Baptist brands
- Map: /territory-map

## Which networks benefit most in the South & Midwest?

**HCA Healthcare** is the clearest multi-state for-profit story in Territory 4 — TriStar in Tennessee, plus Florida and other Sun Belt sites. Name-pattern matching across the national roster finds on the order of **~29** HCA-family TEAM hospitals (including TriStar and HealthONE brands in other territories), the largest single brand cluster we measure.

**AdventHealth** (~16 name-matched TEAM sites) concentrates in Florida and adjacent markets with owned or tightly affiliated ambulatory and post-acute capacity. **Ascension** and various **Baptist** brands add regional density.

Independent hospitals in Nashville, Jacksonville, and Greenville face the classic TEAM problem: high surgical quality with weak leverage over SNF length of stay. Network guides for HCA and AdventHealth unpack the operational playbook.

## What should Territory 4 hospitals prioritize?

Map every TEAM CCN against **HCA and AdventHealth preferred PAC panels** in your CBSA — even if you are not in those systems, your patients may land in the same SNFs. Build competitive home-health capacity for LEJR. Use Florida and Tennessee state guides for named hospital directories, and the episode-volume analysis for procedure mix planning.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many CMS TEAM hospitals are in Territory 4?

164 active hospitals on the March 2026 CMS participant list.

### Which markets matter most?

Nashville (19 hospitals), Jacksonville (13), Memphis (10), and several mid-sized Florida and Carolina CBSAs.

### Is all of Florida in TEAM?

No. CMS selected specific Florida CBSAs. Jacksonville, Daytona/Deltona, Lakeland, and Fort Walton appear; much of Miami was not selected.

### Which network articles should I read?

The HCA Healthcare and AdventHealth CMS TEAM network guides, plus the national hospital-networks advantage overview.

# Named hospitals (live roster)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-directory
hospitals |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, cbsa_label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Hospitals = dplyr::n(),
    `Named hospitals` = paste(hospital, collapse = " · "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(state, dplyr::desc(Hospitals), cbsa_label) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
